answer: Each agent may place one stone on the harbor breakwater. It paints a violet key mark on the stone, attaches a jade tag with its size, and posts a 60-credit bond. The harbor engineer recomputes that layer's required size from the profile; a mismatch burns the bond. Cost grows with the layer: the first stone costs 28, the kth costs 28+7(k-1), so the 1000th costs 7021 and 1000 fakes pay 3,524,500 plus 60,000 in bonds. A rented-stone ring fails: rented stones repeat a violet mark and jade tag. An honest agent pays 28 once and reclaims its bond when clean.
